## Cloud credentials and API URL

`--api-
key` and `--api-url` are declared on `mcpjam cloud` and work before or after descendants (`mcpjam cloud --api-key sk_… eval list`
and `mcpjam cloud eval list --api-key sk_…` are the same). Local commands, including hosted `readiness`, reject those flags at the

program root. Hosted `readiness` still takes leaf `--api-key`.

Credential precedence for Cloud commands:

1. `--api-key` — m
ust be an `sk_` key. A `mcpjam_…` legacy key is a usage error.\n2. `MCPJAM_API_KEY` — same `sk_` rule. A legacy value in this env
var is ignored (with a warning) so SDK eval reporting can still use it.\n3. Stored OAuth from `mcpjam cloud login`\n4. Missing — C
loud commands fail with login guidance before they hit the network (`mcpjam cloud status` reports `missing` instead)\n\nAPI URL pr

ecedence:

1. `--api-url`
2. `MCPJAM_API_URL`, or `MCPJAM_BASE_URL` (the same server without `/api/v1`)
3. The server saved wi
th the OAuth login (only when that login is the credential; a login saved before logins recorded their server counts as MCPJam Clo

ud, and one whose recorded server is not a usable address is refused with exit `3`)
4. `https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1`

Every c
ommand that can contact MCPJam (it accepts `--api-url`, or it uploads results) decides its server when it starts, before it contac
ts anything. An explicit `--api-url`, `MCPJAM_API_URL` or `MCPJAM_BASE_URL` that is not an `http(s)` URL, or that carries credenti
als, a query or a fragment, is a usage error (exit `2`), and so are the two variables naming different servers. The error masks cr
edentials, a query and a fragment, and does not repeat a value that is not a URL. A saved login is only sent to its own server: wh
en it is the credential and the order picks another server, the command exits `3` before any request. `mcpjam cloud status` uses t
he same checks but stays network-free: it still emits the complete JSON report, sets `ok: false`, includes `credential.valid` / `d
eployment.valid` plus an `error` string, and exits `1`. Missing credentials are informational (`credential.valid: null`) and succe
ssful.\n\nSuccessful Cloud commands print an audience line to stderr (`Using MCPJam Cloud as … · project: … · <apiUrl>`). `--quiet

` suppresses it. Machine-readable JSON stays on stdout. `cloud status` redacts API keys.

## Cloud project scope

Most Cloud c

ommands pick one project:

1. `--project <id-or-name>`
2. An explicit `project` field in `--file` / `--json`
3. `MCPJAM_PROJEC

T`
4. The nearest valid `.mcpjam/project.json`

# Local Evals

> Run an MCP

Jam eval suite file on your machine with mcpjam test with local results and an MCPJam identity

> [!NOTE]
>
> The upcoming SDK
10, CLI 6, and Vitest 0.3 releases require an MCPJam login or `sk_` API key for every eval, including BYOK runs with uploads disa
bled. These versions must ship after the backend run-start endpoint is deployed. Earlier versions keep their existing behavior.\n\
n`mcpjam test <file>` runs an MCPJam suite file locally: it connects your MCP servers, drives each case's prompts through a model,
grades the transcript with the same assertions a hosted run uses, and decides the run with the same verdict policy. Bring your ow
n provider key and authenticate the run with MCPJam. With MCPJam-hosted inference it uses your existing CLI login and billing.\n\n
Results are **never uploaded**. The command writes results to your terminal and, if you ask, to a report file. It records the run
start with MCPJam. Like every command, it sends the CLI's single anonymous [telemetry](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/telemetry.md) e
vent, which `--no-telemetry` or `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` turns off; the run adds no telemetry of its own.\n\n## Eval identity and local da
ta\n\nRun `mcpjam cloud login` locally, or set `MCPJAM_API_KEY` to an organization `sk_` key in CI. The SDK also accepts `apiKey`
or `mcpjamAuth` in run options. Explicit credentials take precedence over `MCPJAM_API_KEY`, which takes precedence over the saved
CLI login. An invalid explicit credential never falls back to another account. CI never starts an interactive login. Ask an organi
zation admin for a key if you cannot create one.\n\nEvery logical run needs an online start response. MCPJam retries transient fai
lures within ten seconds, then stops before execution. A prior successful run does not enable offline execution. The CLI resolves
the project using its existing `--project`, environment, and linked-project settings; a key can only access its own organization.\
n\nWith results uploads disabled, the start-run request sends only the credential in the authorization header, any MCPJam API head
ers you configure through the SDK's `inference.resolveMcpjam`, project selection, a new run-start ID, client version and surface (
SDK, CLI, or Vitest), planned iteration count, provider names, and whether a client profile is used (`unknown` for custom executor
s). The server resolves the organization and account. The start-run request sends no prompts, outputs, tool calls, or server URLs.
MCPJam-hosted inference still sends prompts through MCPJam to the model, as before. Retries reuse the same ID. Planned iterations
are intent, not completed usage or a charge. This release adds no debit, quota draw, or balance refusal.\n\n`DO_NOT_TRACK`, `MCPJ
AM_TELEMETRY_DISABLED`, and CLI telemetry settings disable analytics, not the required run-start request. Results remain local unl

ess result uploading is enabled separately.

## Quick start

### 1. Write a suite

Save this as `.mcpjam/evals/example.yaml`

:

```yaml theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
schemaVersion: "2"
mode: agentWorkflow
reportingMode: standard
suite:
 id

: s_notes_example
 name: Notes server
target:
 servers:
 - name: notes
defaults:
 judge:
 enabled: false
 model:

anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5
 iterations: 1
 passThreshold: 1
 validity: {}
cases:
 - id: c_reads_a_note
 title: reads

the note it was asked about
 steps:
 - id: s1
 kind: prompt
 prompt: What does note 7 say?
 - id:

a1
 kind: assert
 assertion:
 type: toolCalledAtLeastOnce
 toolName: read_note
 - id: c_nev

er_deletes
 title: never deletes when only asked to read
 steps:
 - id: s1
 kind: prompt
 prompt: Su

mmarize note 7.
 - id: a1
 kind: assert
 assertion:
 type: toolNeverCalled
 toolName: de
